annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 17-page paper in physical-PDF order, including Sections 1-4, all proofs, algorithms, figures, tables, experiments, conclusions, and references, then compared every candidate with Mathlib and the frozen importable NumStability baseline.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P39 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 17(1), 1996, printed pages 16-32

rejected_candidates.candidate: The standard local convergence facts summarized in Section 1
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly attributes these results to Dembo, Eisenstat, and Steihaug rather than proving them here.

These are source-proved supporting bounds, but each is a short local norm or Taylor-remainder consequence and is below the T3 difficulty floor. No compiled NumStability result makes any one of them a valid T1 task.

This theorem is source-backed and unavailable in the compiled library, but Theorem 2.3's final R-order argument supplies a cleaner and harder self-contained T3 core with an explicit substantial induction.

rejected_candidates.candidate: The squared Choice 1 rate following Theorem 2.2
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly states this result without proof.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithm INB global convergence and GMRES properties in Section 3.1
rejected_candidates.reason: The convergence theorem is quoted from an earlier Eisenstat--Walker paper and GMRES is imported from Saad--Schultz; P39 does not prove these results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Safeguards, test problems, numerical comparisons, and conclusions in Sections 2.1-4
rejected_candidates.reason: These are algorithm choices, empirical observations, and qualitative recommendations rather than new source-proved universal theorem statements.

T1.decision: Skipped. The compiled NumStability set has no inexact-Newton, nonlinear local-convergence, forcing-term, or q/r-order theorem, so no complete source-proved result receives exactly one substantial library shortcut.

T2.decision: Skipped. No P39 proof needs at least two distinct substantial results from the compiled NumStability set; the relevant nonlinear convergence material is entirely absent from that set.

T3.decision: Selected the R-order part of Theorem 2.3 for gamma=1, specialized to the paper's tested value alpha=2 after the exact reindexing on printed page 22. The task retains the residual recurrence, smallness condition, scaling, simultaneous product induction, doubly exponential bound, and convergence conclusion.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions whose statements and supporting derivations appear in this paper.
Do not turn the cited standard inexact-Newton, globalized-backtracking, or GMRES results into P39 tasks.
Treat the alpha=2, gamma=1 case as a specialization of the parameter range explicitly proved and used in the experiments, not as a new theorem.
Do not count uncompiled Chapter-25 nonlinear-system source files as available to condition L.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
